source.title: Sequential Group Composition: A Window into the Mechanics of Deep Learning
source.authors: Giovanni Luca Marchetti; Daniel Kunin; Adele Myers; Francisco Acosta; N. Miolane

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training dynamics for the emergence of Fourier features in group-composition tasks. This tests the gradual feature-formation aspect of V2 with a different task scope and analysis, but it does not test grokking or delayed train-to-test generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Fourier-feature learning dynamics relevant to V2. It does not report the train/test accuracy trajectory, overfitting, memorizing-component removal, or generalization jump in the claim. Its width-scaling results and constructive RNN/MLP solutions concern efficiency and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains on the full dataset: all |G|^k sequences, or fresh online samples, with no held-out split. It reports only training-loss staircases and Fourier/irrep power. There is no train/test gap, no delayed generalization, and no memorizing component, so no grokking version is tested. Its stepwise feature-acquisition results are a related construct (saddle-to-saddle feature learning) and are recorded under fits_no_version. Power et al. and Nanda et al. are cited only as related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors prove that two-layer networks from vanishing initialization learn sequential group composition one irrep at a time, in an order set by the encoding's Fourier statistics. They show such networks need width exponential in k, and construct RNN and deep-MLP solutions with width constant in k. They caution that the deep results are constructive, not proofs that gradient descent finds them.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses full finite-group sequence-composition tasks, orbit-based encodings, mean-squared loss, and Fourier/AGF analysis. It does not use the small train/test split and delayed test-generalization setup in the original grokking studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Irrep acquisition order depends on encoding Fourier statistics and irrep dimension; the gap between learning two D3 irreps increases with sequence length; stepwise behavior varies with initialization scale and activation.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer polynomial (and ReLU, some Tanh/GeLU) networks trained from small initialization on full-data group composition acquire irreps one at a time. The order is set by the encoding's Fourier statistics, and a lower-dimensional-irrep bias grows with sequence length. The stepwise behaviour weakens at larger initialization scale and for activations lacking the degree-k Taylor term.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under small initialization, networks learning group composition acquire Fourier features stepwise, one irrep at a time, in an order set by encoding statistics and irrep dimension.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The experiments are on synthetic group-composition tasks and do not evaluate held-out generalization or grokking. Several relevant values are shown only in plots, without numerical estimates or uncertainty. The two-layer dynamical theory assumes vanishing initialization and includes an alignment assumption; the deep-network constructions do not establish that gradient descent finds them.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 reports width, group-size, and training-loss scaling, while Figure 5 and Sections 5.1-5.2 report recurrent-network structure and constructive depth results. These do not measure any claim version's grokking or delayed-generalization behavior.

untested.parts: All: there is no held-out set, train/test accuracy delay or training-set-size sweep.
All: no generalizing-versus-memorizing circuit, no removal of memorization, and no progress measures predicting a test-accuracy jump.
All: no non-algorithmic data, and the initialization-scale effect is on stepwise training dynamics, not delayed generalization.
All: no weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
All: there is no cross-run algorithm comparison. The theory predicts irrep-based solutions but does not test convergence across runs.
All: no optimizer or floating-point artifact controls.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 and its V2 labels are rejected. The experiments use the full dataset or online sampling, so generalization beyond overfitting cannot occur. The feature emergence is abrupt and stepwise on training loss, which is a distinct phenomenon from grokking's delayed test-accuracy jump.

versions.untested_parts: No small training-set versus test-set experiment, overfitting-to-generalization trajectory, or training-set-size sweep.

The study measures gradual acquisition of task-relevant Fourier irreps, but does not measure memorizing components being removed, a grokking jump in test accuracy, or whether progress measures predict such a jump.
No non-algorithmic data or lazy-to-rich transition in grokking-like generalization is tested.
No realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
No weight-decay or low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking experiment.
The study does not compare runs to determine whether they converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
No optimizer-instability or floating-point artifact challenge.

rows.value: figure only; the text states that irreps are learned one at a time in order determined by their importance to the encoding

rows.check: Full-data training-loss and irrep-power trajectory; no generalization, memorization or test-accuracy jump. Feature acquisition is stepwise (abrupt drops), not the gradual circuit formation beneath a grokking jump that V2 names.

rows.subject: two-layer network
rows.operation_detail: Track power in the one-dimensional sign irrep and two-dimensional rotation irrep over training.
rows.measure: Time between learning the sign and rotation irrep
rows.value: figure only; the text states that the time between learning the one-dimensional sign irrep and the two-dimensional rotation irrep increases as k gets larger
rows.note: This is a sequence-length effect on irrep acquisition, not a training-set-size effect or a test-accuracy delay.
rows.check: The sequence-length effect on the interval between learning two irreps is not a generalization delay. Initialization scale and learning rate also change across k (Section D.2), so the comparison is confounded.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Binary group composition in the groups shown in Figure 3; D3 sequence-length sweep; small-initialization and activation settings with sequential irrep acquisition
reader_labels.reason: Irrep power and neuron Fourier energy show staged, ordered feature acquisition; the reported interval between two irreps increases with sequence length (R1-R11). This supports gradual Fourier-feature formation, not the full grokking mechanism.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Larger initialization and the Tanh k = 2 and GeLU k = 3 activation conditions
reader_labels.reason: Stepwise acquisition is weaker at the larger initialization scale, and these activation conditions show more simultaneous irrep learning rather than the analyzed ordering (R6, R12-R13).
